- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast windows, especially after recent spikes; apply downward bias correction for first 5–7 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model tends to overshoot and fail to correct — reduce forecast slope in subsequent days.
- When sentiment history is flat (all 0.00), model exhibits high volatility bias — dampen forecast variance and favor mean-reversion toward recent 7-day average.
- If true outcome shows rapid downward trend after a peak, model often fails to recognize it — add early warning lag correction: if 3-day moving average of true values declines, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day.
- In absence of sentiment signals, model overweights recent history — reduce weight of last 3–5 days in smoothing window for longer-term forecasts.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture late-cycle corrections — apply “tail correction”: if last 3 days of true values are below 10% of 30-day mean, reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3 days.
